claims.statement: The EU Payment Observatory's 2025 annual report says more than half of EU companies reported difficulties from late payments in 2024 and suppliers reported average B2B and government-to-business payment periods above 60 days.
The same report identifies pursuing late payments as a significant administrative burden, supporting workflow pain but not a software purchase budget.
Invoice and bank data could predict and prioritize collection work, but the incremental recovery over ordinary reminders must be demonstrated experimentally.
Reachable Polish invoice volume, debtor-data legality and willingness to pay a success fee are unknown.

contrary_evidence: Accounting systems, collection agencies, factors and trade-credit insurers already address parts of the workflow.
Payment delay can reflect a genuine dispute or insolvency that better reminders cannot solve.
A cross-customer debtor graph raises confidentiality, GDPR, accuracy and possible credit-scoring concerns.

economics.acquisition_route: Embed through accounting offices, KSeF integrators, SME banks, factoring brokers and trade-credit insurers rather than relying on founder-led outbound sales.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: With lawful permissions, an anonymized record of payer timing, invoice features, reminder sequence and recovery outcome can improve prioritization and reveal which intervention works for each segment.
fingerprint.customer: Polish B2B SMEs issuing roughly 50 to 500 invoices per month, especially exporters and construction, logistics or health suppliers whose owners or finance teams manually chase receivables.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed through accounting offices, KSeF integrators, SME banks, factoring brokers and trade-credit insurers rather than relying on founder-led outbound sales.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Connect KSeF or accounting exports and bank transactions, score expected payment timing, automate respectful evidence-backed reminders, track promises to pay and route only unresolved cases to a human, collection partner or factor. Separate prediction from any regulated credit decision.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The supplier would pay per entity per month plus a percentage of overdue cash collected after the workflow starts; factoring or legal handoff can pay a referral fee where disclosed. Recurring late-payment pain is evidenced, but recurring willingness to buy this specific layer is not.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A due date approaches or passes, an expected payment is missing and staff must decide whom to contact, what evidence to attach, when to escalate and whether to use legal collection or factoring without harming the customer relationship.

founder_fit: Strong finance, data-science and automation alignment.
KSeF creates a Poland-specific data-access wedge that can later generalize to EU e-invoicing.
Outcome pricing and accounting-channel distribution support part-time validation.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: KSeF-connected late-payment early warning and recovery workflow
uncertainties: Incremental cash recovery and days-sales-outstanding improvement versus a disciplined manual baseline.
Whether KSeF and bank permissions are acceptable to accounting offices and their clients.
Customer concentration, dispute incidence and legal-collection conversion economics.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Run a permissioned shadow study over at least 5,000 invoices from 10 SMEs, then randomize eligible overdue invoices between the existing process and a human-approved automated sequence. Charge only a share of incremental cash collected inside a fixed window and stop if relationship complaints or disputed-invoice escalation rises.
